content.title: About
content.content: Pompano (Trachinotus ovatus) is a marine fish from the jack family, native to warm waters of the Indo‑Pacific region. The fillet has a delicate, slightly sweet flavor, firm white flesh and a moderate fat content, making it popular in both restaurants and home cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pompano is often called the “golden fish” because of its golden‑orange hue.
The species grows quickly, reaching up to 30 cm in length and 1.5 kg in weight within a year.
In Japan, pompano is considered a delicacy and is frequently used in sushi rolls.
Pompano is rich in omega‑3 fatty acids, which are beneficial for heart health.
In the wild, pompano migrates to coastal lagoons for spawning.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids help lower cholesterol levels and support cardiovascular function.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Pompano fillet provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, aiding muscle building and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The fish contains vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, essential for metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Pompano supplies selenium, phosphorus and potassium, supporting immunity and electrolyte balance.

items.title: Low mercury levels
items.content: Compared with larger predatory fish, pompano has lower mercury, making it safe for regular consumption.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, including pompano.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the fish has been pre‑marinated or processed, sodium levels can be high.

items.title: Possible parasites
items.content: As with any raw fish, pompano should be thoroughly cooked to eliminate potential parasites.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pompano fillet can be grilled, baked, steamed, or used in sushi. To keep it tender, cook at a moderate temperature of 180‑200 °C for 12‑15 minutes, depending on thickness. Season with lemon, herbs, olive oil or soy sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh fillet in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C in an airtight container for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C in a vacuum‑sealed bag; the fish retains quality for up to 3 months. Thaw frozen fillet in the refrigerator before cooking.
